per_sample.question: How many working days of annual leave do employees get, and how many days can be carried over into the next year?
per_sample.answer:
- Employees are entitled to 24 working days of annual leave per year [Acme_Employee_Handbook_2026.pdf, Page 4, Lines 1-11].
- Up to 8 days of unused annual leave may be carried over into the next leave year [Acme_Employee_Handbook_2026.pdf, Page 4, Lines 3-19].

The following leave types and annual entitlements apply to all confirmed employees:
Leave entitlements are pro-rated in the joining year and in the year of exit.
Carry-over: up to 8 days of unused annual leave may be carried into the next leave year; carried-over
leave expires on 31 March of that year. Sick leave and casual leave cannot be carried over under any
circumstances.
Annual leave of 3 or more consecutive working days requires 14 calendar days of advance notice and
manager approval recorded in the HR portal. Leave taken without approval is treated as loss of pay.
Sick leave of more than 3 consecutive working days must be supported by a registered medical
practitioner's certificate submitted within 5 working days of rejoining.

4. Leave Policy
The leave year runs from 1 January to 31 December. All leave must be applied for in the HR portal before
it is taken, except in emergencies covered by sick leave rules below.
The following leave types and annual entitlements apply to all confirmed employees:
Leave type | Entitlement per year | Advance notice | Carry-over
Annual / earned leave | 24 working days | 14 calendar days for 3+ day blocks | Up to 8 days, expires 31 March
Sick leave | 12 working days | Inform manager same day; certificate if 3+ days | Not allowed
Casual leave | 6 working days | 2 working days | Not allowed
Maternity leave | 26 weeks | As per Maternity Benefit Act; max 8 weeks prenatal | Not applicable
Paternity leave | 4 weeks | 7 calendar days | Not applicable; within 6 months of birth
Bereavement leave | 5 working days | Retroactive application within 7 working days | Not applicable

11. Separation and Exit
Resignation must be submitted through the HR portal. The notice period is 30 calendar days for Grades L1
and L2, and 60 calendar days for Grades L3 and above. Notice pay in lieu is permitted only with mutual
written agreement.
During the notice period the employee is expected to complete a structured handover documented in the
handover template; the relieving letter is issued only after the reporting manager signs off the handover.
Full and final settlement, including reimbursements and leave encashment (annual leave only, capped at
45 days), is processed within 45 calendar days of the last working day.
All company assets (laptop, access cards, and peripherals) must be returned on or before the last working
day; unreturned assets are recovered at book value from the settlement amount.
per_sample.reference: Employees get 24 working days of annual leave per year. Up to 8 unused days may be carried into the next leave year, and carried-over leave expires on 31 March.

per_sample.question: What is the per-night hotel ceiling for a Grade L3 employee travelling within India, and what flight class are they entitled to?

per_sample.question: What is the minimum password length and the password rotation period?
per_sample.answer:
- The minimum password length is 12 characters minimum [Acme_IT_Security_Policy_2026.pdf, Page 2, Lines 1-13].

This office-attendance requirement remains unchanged under the 2026 addendum [Acme_Remote_Work_Addendum_A_2026.pdf, Page 1, Lines 11-12]. per_sample.answer:
No, Restricted data cannot be accessed from a personal device. [Acme_IT_Security_Policy_2026.pdf, Page 3, Lines 1-10]
The policy explicitly states that Confidential and Restricted resources require a corporate device. [Acme_IT_Security_Policy_2026.pdf, Page 3, Lines 1-10]

contexts:
13. Data Handling Cross-Reference
All employee and customer personal data referenced in this Handbook is classified and handled according
to the Acme Corp IT Security Policy 2026, including the data classification scheme (Public, Internal,
Confidential, Restricted) defined there.
HR records are Confidential; identity documents, salary information, and health records are Restricted and
may be accessed only by named HR roles listed in the HR data register.
Suspected data breaches involving HR records must be reported to security@acme.example within 24
hours under the incident response procedure of the IT Security Policy.
Acme Corp — Internal / Confidential
Page 13

3. Device Security
Full-disk encryption (FileVault or BitLocker) is mandatory on all laptops and mobile devices used for Acme
Corp work, including personal devices under the BYOD programme.
Devices must auto-lock after 5 minutes of inactivity with a password or biometric unlock. Critical OS and
browser patches must be applied within 72 hours of release; all other security patches within 14 days.
Loss or theft of any device with access to corporate systems must be reported to security@acme.example
and the IT helpdesk within 24 hours; the device is remotely wiped and all stored sessions revoked.
Personal devices may access Internal-classification resources only through the managed browser;
Confidential and Restricted resources require a corporate device.
Acme Corp — Internal / Confidential
Page 3

4. Data Classification
All data must be classified at creation into one of four levels:
Level | Definition | Examples | Handling rule
Public | Approved for public release | Marketing material, job postings | No restriction
Internal | Default for business data | This policy, org charts | Employees and approved contractors
Confidential | Damage to Acme Corp if disclosed | Contracts, financials, HR records | Need-to-know; encrypted sharing
Restricted | Severe legal/financial harm if disclosed | Customer PII, health records, credentials | Named-access only; secure-share portal
Personally identifiable information (PII) of employees and customers is Restricted by default. Restricted
data must be encrypted at rest and in transit, and shared only through the approved secure-share portal —
never as email attachments.

3. Working Hours and Attendance
The standard work week is 45 hours, Monday to Friday. Core hours during which every office-based
employee must be reachable are 10:00 to 16:00 India Standard Time; flexible band hours are 07:00 to

9. Performance Management
The performance year runs from 1 April to 31 March. Every employee has documented quarterly check-ins
with their manager in the performance portal, and a formal annual review in April.
Ratings are: Exceptional, Exceeds Expectations, Meets Expectations, Needs Improvement, and
Unsatisfactory. A rating of Needs Improvement places the employee on a Performance Improvement Plan
(PIP) of up to 60 days with fortnightly reviews.
Promotions are effective in the April and October cycles. Eligibility requires a rating of Meets Expectations
or higher in the most recent cycle, completion of 12 months in the current grade, and a current-year
promotion budget confirmation from Finance.

The following leave types and annual entitlements apply to all confirmed employees:
Leave entitlements are pro-rated in the joining year and in the year of exit.
Carry-over: up to 8 days of unused annual leave may be carried into the next leave year; carried-over
leave expires on 31 March of that year. Sick leave and casual leave cannot be carried over under any
circumstances.
Annual leave of 3 or more consecutive working days requires 14 calendar days of advance notice and
manager approval recorded in the HR portal. Leave taken without approval is treated as loss of pay.
Sick leave of more than 3 consecutive working days must be supported by a registered medical
practitioner's certificate submitted within 5 working days of rejoining.

6. Access Control
Access follows least privilege and role-based access control. Access requests are raised in the identity
portal, approved by the system owner, and granted within 2 business days for standard roles.
Access rights are reviewed quarterly by system owners; unused accounts are disabled after 45 days of
inactivity and deleted after 90 days.
Leavers lose all access on their last working day (same-day revocation by IT upon HR trigger). Privileged
(administrator) access requires a named individual, a justification, and automatic expiry after 90 days.

10. Benefits Summary
All regular employees are covered by group health insurance with a family floater sum insured of 500,000
INR. Employees at Grade L3 and above receive a top-up cover of 200,000 INR. New joiners are enrolled
automatically on their start date.
An annual preventive health check-up is covered for employees aged 40 and above, and for all employees
at Grade L3 and above, up to 6,000 INR per year.
The learning and development budget is 30,000 INR per year for Grades L2 and above, usable for
courses, certifications, and books with manager approval; it does not carry over.
Group term life insurance of 24 months of fixed pay and personal accident cover of 12 months of fixed pay
apply to all regular employees at no cost.
Statutory benefits (provident fund, gratuity, and insurance under the ESI Act where applicable) are
administered per law and summarized on each payslip.

11. Separation and Exit
Resignation must be submitted through the HR portal. The notice period is 30 calendar days for Grades L1
and L2, and 60 calendar days for Grades L3 and above. Notice pay in lieu is permitted only with mutual
written agreement.
During the notice period the employee is expected to complete a structured handover documented in the
handover template; the relieving letter is issued only after the reporting manager signs off the handover.
Full and final settlement, including reimbursements and leave encashment (annual leave only, capped at
45 days), is processed within 45 calendar days of the last working day.
All company assets (laptop, access cards, and peripherals) must be returned on or before the last working
day; unreturned assets are recovered at book value from the settlement amount.

8. Expense and Travel Policy
All business expenses must be genuine, business-related, supported by original invoices, and submitted
through the expense portal within 30 calendar days of the expense date. Late submissions beyond 60
days are reimbursed only with CFO approval.
Travel class and hotel ceilings by grade are as follows (per night, within India):
Grade | Flight class | Hotel ceiling (per night, India) | Local travel
L1 | Economy | 4,000 INR | Cab, actuals
L2 | Premium economy | 7,000 INR | Cab, actuals
L3 | Business | 12,000 INR | Chauffeur for client meetings
L4 (Director+) | Business | 18,000 INR | Chauffeur
The meal allowance on business travel within India is 600 INR per day (no receipts required). Incidental
expenses are covered at 100 INR per day.
Any single expense above 25,000 INR requires pre-approval from the Chief Financial Officer in addition to
the normal manager approval.
